sentences.text: Europa Clipper drops by home one last time on its way to Jupiter: flying past Earth, it steals speed from the planet's gravity.

The spacecraft is moving faster than twelve kilometres a second relative to Earth and will come within three thousand two hundred kilometres of the surface; that is lower than many communications satellites.
Closest approach is at twenty fifteen universal time; the flyby stretches the craft's orbit around the Sun far enough to reach Jupiter.
Clipper will arrive at Jupiter in April 2030 and study the ocean beneath Europa's icy shell over forty-nine close flybys.
The trajectory data comes from NASA/JPL Horizons, sampled at one-minute resolution around closest approach.
